role: Agent 2, first-time user comprehension: can a person who has never seen the panel tell, folded and open, which theme the key draws and whether it is its own or the shared one, find the other themes, and read the folded chip correctly.
environment: Simulated host only: pi-sim.mjs from C:\Users\stephen\git\hwinfo-pi-density (production plugin modules via npx tsx) serving d04, A, B, C and my review copy A2; headless Chrome via cdp.mjs. Ports 34020/34021/34022 (lab.mjs) and 34023/34024/34025 (lab2.mjs), one variant at a time. Widths 373 and 320 at DPR 1.5, 189 and 160 at DPR 3, height 410. States: key Default on Void, key on a Paper shared theme, key Ultraviolet, key Graphite, key with unknown stored theme "neon-2031", empty key on Paper, dial Ember, empty dial; open and folded; pointer clicks, Tab/Enter/Space, Fold all, Open all, Alt-click, remembered fold on the next key, empty key and dial, live pick and shared-theme change while folded, a 250 ms fold-answer delay; accessible names from the CDP accessibility tree. No Stream Deck app, no HWiNFO, no installed plugin, no port 23654, no computer use. Scripts and results: C:\Users\stephen\AppData\Local\Temp\hw-tf-beginner\lab.mjs, lab2.mjs, shots\results-d04A.json, results-BC.json, results-A2.json, lab2-ABC.json, lab2-A2.json. I am an AI reviewer; nothing here is user research.

verdicts.reasons: Best first-time reading of the three. Folded, the row is recognizably a section like the others: the title has the same computed style as Reading (13px, weight 600, rgb(236,236,236)), and the scope text uses the same muted summary idiom as every other folded section. Open, the status line and Change are outside the toggle, so clicking the line does nothing and a 2 px miss left of Change lands on inert text. Blocking: (1) BT01, the 22 px folded chip does not read as the chip. Its accent bar starts 2.1 px above the bottom of the text line box (in the grid chip the bar clears it by 0.9 px), so the folded chip reads as underlined link text in a link-like blue, with a chain glyph on Default. (2) BT02, on a key with no reading the folded row shows the Paper chip beside a black 'Pick a sensor' face, and the only sentence that reconciles them folds away. Cost: open band 130 px against 106 in d04 and 113 in B/C.

verdicts.reasons: What sets B apart from C is the 22 px folded chip, and that chip is the defect. The accent bar overlaps the text line box by 2.1 px, so 'Default', 'Void' or 'Ember' reads as an underlined link (MEASURED, zoomed capture). Fixing it turns B into C. B also shares C's comprehension costs: 'Theme' is an 11.5px, weight 400, muted label, while every other folded row has a 13px, weight 600 title, so in the all-folded list Theme reads as a caption rather than a section. Clicking the open status line folds the palette (MEASURED clickOpenLineFolds true). A miss 2 px left of or below Change folds it too (MEASURED left2 and below2 both hit the summary). Like every variant, it hides the empty-key sentence when folded.
verdicts.evidence: MEASURED shots\results-BC.json B.tests (clickOpenLineFolds true, changeHit left2/below2 'summary'); MEASURED B title style in states['key-default@373'].folded.title vs readingTitle; lab2-ABC.json B.miniGap.gap -2.1; captures shots\B-zoom-folded-row.png, B-zoom-folded-row-void.png, B-key-all-folded-373.png (brief shots), B-key-empty-paper-373-folded.png.

verdicts.reasons: The folded chip matches the grid chip: face 83 x 30, bar clear of the text by 1.9 px. A newcomer sees the same object they just picked, not a link. The row stays compact open (113 px). Blocking: BT02, the same empty-key contradiction as A and B. Not blocking, but my reasons for preferring A: the muted 'Theme' label is weaker than the other section titles in the folded list; clicking the open status line folds the palette; a near miss on Change folds it; and folded it is 76 px at 160 px wide. If C is chosen, style the label as a section title at least while folded, and accept the toggle-on-line behavior knowingly.

required_changes.change: Draw the folded chip at the grid chip's geometry instead of the 22 px mini, meaning the same object as in the grid. CSS: details .hw-look-mini .hw-theme-face { height: 30px; min-width: 83px; padding: 0 6px; } and details .hw-look-mini .hw-theme-spark { left: 8px; right: 8px; bottom: 3px; }. The cleaner route is to reuse the .hw-look .hw-theme-face and .hw-look .hw-theme-spark rules for the mini. Keep the dashed frame and link mark on Default, both drawn in the resolved palette. Tried in my review copy C:\Users\stephen\AppData\Local\Temp\hw-tf-beginner\proto-A2 (proto-A.css tail). If the density reviewers reject the 8 px, a 26 px face with the value lifted 2 px (padding-bottom 4px) should pass the same gap test. That fallback is INFERRED, not measured.
required_changes.why: MEASURED: in A and B the accent bar's top sits 2.1 px above the bottom of the value's line box. In the grid chip it sits 0.9 px below, in C 1.9 px below. The bar therefore sits under the glyphs like an underline. Void's accent rgb(76,194,255) is close to the link color rgb(142,203,255), and Default adds a chain glyph, so a newcomer sees 'Default' as a hyperlink and expects navigation, when clicking opens the band (WH on the misread, MEASURED on the geometry). The owner asked for the selected theme's chip, and the chip in the grid is the object a person learns. With BT01 the folded band is 43 px at 373 and 81 px at 160.
required_changes.acceptance_test: On the simulated host at 373 and 160 px, fold the band for key Default on Void, key Default on Paper, key Void and dial Ember. For each, measure (spark top minus the value's line-box bottom) in the folded chip and in the grid chip: the folded value must be >= 0.9 px and within 1 px of the grid value. The face must be 30 px tall and >= 83 px wide. documentElement scrollWidth must equal clientWidth. A 3x zoomed capture must show the bar separated from the text as in the grid chip (lab2.mjs does this; results-A2 passes: gap 0.9, 83 x 30, overflow 0).

required_changes.change: On a key with no reading, the folded row says the theme is not on the key yet. Append ' · shows once a reading is picked' to the folded summary text (#theme-sum in A) so it is part of the summary's accessible name. Drive it in renderThemeLine/renderThemeHelp from the same 'configured' test that sets the help line. Do not match on help text as my prototype copy does. A dial never gets the note, because its prompt is drawn in its theme (pi-common.js 3917-3923). The unknown-theme help sentence can stay open-only, because the folded row already says 'unknown; draws X'.
required_changes.why: RD/MEASURED in every variant: the help line 'Shows on the key once a reading is picked.' folds away with the band. The folded row then shows a cream Paper chip beside a black 'Pick a sensor' face. The fold memory carries a fold made on a configured key to the next new empty key (rememberedEmptyKey true), so this is the normal path, not a corner case. It breaks the owner's rule that the resolved theme stays visible and truthful folded, and a first-time user reads it as 'the theme did not apply'.
required_changes.acceptance_test: Fixture key-empty with globals theme paper, band folded (directly and via a fold remembered from key-configured). The summary's visible text and its AX name must read 'Theme Default (shared: Paper) · shows once a reading is picked', with no horizontal overflow at 373, 189 and 160 (A2 measured: 45 px at 373, 113.5 px at 160, overflow 0). dial-empty folded must read 'Theme Default (shared: Void)' with no note (A2 measured). Picking a reading while folded must drop the note and leave the band folded.

answers.q1_variant: A, with BT01 (chip at grid size, taken from C) and BT02 (empty-key note). Folded, a newcomer answers 'what is drawn and where does it come from' from three things on one row. The title matches the other sections, so the row reads as a section. The chip is the same object as in the grid, drawn in the palette the key uses; Default keeps its dashed frame and link mark. The scope words '(shared: Void)' or '(set on this key)' are the same words as the open line. The header face stays the ground truth above it. Open, A reads the most conventionally: section title, a status line with Change, then eight named chips. It is also the only variant where clicking the status line or missing Change cannot fold the palette (MEASURED). Cost: the open band is 130 px (d04 106, B/C 113), and folded it is 43 px at 373 and 81 px at 160 (MEASURED A2). If the owner weighs the 17 px open saving over these points, C plus BT02 plus a section-title label while folded is the fallback; B should not ship as is.
answers.q2_fold_all: Yes: Open all, Fold all and Alt-click should include the band, as all three prototypes already do (MEASURED foldAllFoldsTheme, openAllOpensTheme and altClickFoldsTheme all true; with only the theme band open, Fold all stays live with aria-disabled false). The buttons' names are 'Open all sections' and 'Fold all sections'. A band that folds like a section but ignores 'all' would make the word false and teach a wrong model of the panel. Nothing about the drawn theme is lost, because the folded row keeps the chip and scope (MEASURED in the all-folded capture).
answers.q3_hidden_until_answer: Acceptable. MEASURED with a 250 ms plugin reply: A, B and C hide the band until about 370-400 ms after navigation, where d04 painted it from the first 75 ms sample. The pinned header with the key face is not a .hw-sec and stays visible, so the panel is never blank. The band arrives in the same paint as the sections under it. The alternative would paint a remembered fold open and then collapse it, pulling everything below up by about 80 px under the pointer, which is worse for a newcomer. For a first-time user the default is open, so nothing moves either way.
answers.q4_accessibility: The folded summary is the native disclosure (CDP role DisclosureTriangle, expanded false; MEASURED). Its accessible name must equal its visible text (WCAG 2.5.3 Label in Name): 'Theme Default (shared: Void)', 'Theme Ember (set on this dial)', 'Theme "neon-2031" (unknown; draws Void)', plus the BT02 note on an empty key. All of these were MEASURED in A, B and C, except the note, which exists only in A2. Open, A's name is 'Theme', expanded true, matching the other sections, whose summary text hides when open; B/C keep the value in the name. The folded chip must stay a plain span: not focusable, no radio role, no label of its own (true in all three). The extra Tab stop is justified: a fold must be keyboard operable (WCAG 2.1.1), and the APG Disclosure pattern puts the disclosure button in the Tab sequence. MEASURED order open: Open all toolbar, theme summary, Change, checked chip (4 stops, d04 had 3). Folded, Tab goes from the theme summary straight to the Reading summary, so a folded user saves 2 stops. Enter folds and Space reopens (MEASURED).
answers.q5_edge_states: No reading, key: every variant hides 'Shows on the key once a reading is picked.' when folded, and the remembered fold reaches new empty keys (MEASURED), so the folded Paper chip contradicts the black 'Pick a sensor' face. BT02 fixes it (A2 MEASURED 45 px at 373, 113.5 px at 160, no overflow). No reading, dial: the prompt is drawn in the theme, so no note is needed (READ; A2 MEASURED no note). Unknown stored theme: the folded row is text only, '"neon-2031" (unknown; draws Void)', with no chip. That is honest, because no chip is checked when open either, and it names what is drawn. Keep it wrapping, not ellipsized (A wraps: 65 px at 160, overflow 0, MEASURED). Its help sentence may fold away. Paper shared theme: the folded Default chip is cream with a dashed frame in Paper's label color and reads clearly on the dark panel (captured A2 and A). Live while folded: picking Forest and then folding shows Forest; changing the shared theme to Paper in Advanced while folded updates the chip to Paper's background and the text to '(shared: Paper)' (MEASURED, one global write). At 200% zoom (189 and 160 px), no variant overflows horizontally, open or folded (MEASURED overflowX 0). Folded heights: A2 61/81 px, A 53/73, B 50/50, C 58/76. Open heights are about 217-241 px.

keep: Band open by default on first open; fold remembered per panel kind in the plugin's RAM like every other section (sec-theme fits the id pattern; the key and dial panels use 10 of the 12 remembered ids, READ)
Clicking the folded chip opens the band (MEASURED in A, B, C): the chip looks clickable and clicking it gives a person who wants another theme exactly what they need
Default's dashed frame and link mark on the folded chip, drawn in the resolved shared palette
The same scope words folded and open: '(shared: X)', '(set on this key)', '(set on this dial)', '(unknown; draws X)'
Change kept outside the summary, never a control inside it (folded it is not painted, not hit-testable and not in the Tab order, MEASURED)
Open all, Fold all and Alt-click include the band, and aria-disabled counts it
The band hidden with the other sections until the fold answer, header face always visible
The folded row follows picks and shared-theme changes live (MutationObserver in proto.js)
Folded summary accessible name equals its visible text; the chip is a plain span with no role and no Tab stop
No selection ring on the folded chip: there are no options beside it, so the ring would mean nothing
